Failure to flush is logged but never blocks shutdown.\n1935\t\n1936\t## OpenTelemetry Semantic Mapping\n1937\t\n1938\tNEEDLE's existing event catalog maps cleanly to OpenTelemetry's three signal types. This mapping is **normative** — the OTLP sink implementation must conform to it so dashboards and alerts remain stable across NEEDLE versions.\n1939\t\n1940\t### Resource Attributes\n1941\t\n1942\tEvery exported signal carries these resource attributes (per OTel semantic conventions):\n1943\t\n1944\t| Attribute | Value | Source |\n1945\t|-----------|-------|--------|\n1946\t| `service.name` | `\"needle\"` | Constant |\n1947\t| `service.version` | build version | `env!(\"CARGO_PKG_VERSION\")` |\n1948\t| `service.instance.id` | `<worker_id>` | e.g., `needle-claude-anthropic-sonnet-alpha` |\n1949\t| `service.namespace` | `\"needle-fleet\"` (default, configurable) | Config |\n1950\t| `deployment.environment` | e.g., `\"production\"` | Config |\n1951\t| `host.name` | hostname | OS |\n1952\t| `process.pid` | worker PID | OS |\n1953\t| `needle.agent` | e.g., `\"claude-anthropic-sonnet\"` | Worker config |\n1954\t| `needle.model` | e.g., `\"claude-sonnet-4-6\"` | Worker config |\n1955\t| `needle.session_id` | session ID | Per-boot random |\n1956\t| `needle.workspace` | workspace path | Worker config |\n1957\t\n1958\t### Traces\n1959\t\n1960\tThe NEEDLE state machine is naturally hierarchical, which maps directly to OTel spans.\n1961\t\n1962\t```\n1963\tworker.session                                          (root span, lifetime = worker process)\n1964\t├── strand.pluck                                        (one per strand evaluation)\n1965\t│   └── bead.lifecycle                                  (one per claimed bead)\n1966\t│       ├── bead.claim                                  (ATOMIC phase)\n1967\t│       ├── bead.prompt_build\n1968\t│       ├── agent.dispatch                              (DISPATCHING + EXECUTING)\n1969\t│       │   └── agent.execution                         (process alive; span.ok on exit 0)\n1970\t│       └── bead.outcome                                (HANDLING)\n1971\t│           └── bead.mitosis?                           (optional, if outcome = failure)\n1972\t├── strand.mend\n1973\t├── strand.explore\n1974\t├── strand.weave\n1975\t├── strand.unravel\n1976\t├── strand.pulse\n1977\t└── strand.knot                                         (terminal backoff / exhaustion)\n1978\t```\n1979\t\n1980\tSpan naming follows OpenTelemetry conventions: lowercase dotted, verb-form where appropriate.\n1981\t\n1982\t**Span attributes** follow OTel semantic conventions where applicable, plus a `needle.*` namespace:\n1983\t\n1984\t| Span | Key Attributes |\n1985\t|------|----------------|\n1986\t| `worker.session` | `needle.beads_processed`, `needle.uptime_seconds`, `needle.exit_reason` |\n1987\t| `strand.*` | `needle.strand.name`, `needle.strand.result`, `needle.strand.duration_ms` |\n1988\t| `bead.lifecycle` | `needle.bead.id`, `needle.bead.priority`, `needle.bead.title_hash`, `needle.bead.outcome` |\n1989\t| `bead.claim` | `needle.claim.retry_number`, `needle.claim.result` (`succeeded` / `race_lost` / `failed`) |\n1990\t| `agent.dispatch` | `gen_ai.system` (e.g., `anthropic`), `gen_ai.request.model`, `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens`, `gen_ai.usage.output_tokens`, `needle.agent.pid`, `needle.agent.exit_code` |\n1991\t| `bead.outcome` | `needle.outcome` (`success` / `failure` / `timeout` / `crash` / `agent_not_found` / `interrupted`), `needle.outcome.action` |\n1992\t\n1993\t**GenAI semantic conventions.** The `agent.dispatch` span uses OTel's `gen_ai.*` conventions so NEEDLE's token/cost data shows up in GenAI dashboards out-of-the-box (Grafana GenAI app, Langfuse, Honeycomb AI, etc.).\n1994\t\n1995\t**Span status.** Success outcomes set `Status::Ok`. All other outcomes set `Status::Error` with a description matching the `needle.outcome` value. This makes error-rate SLOs trivial.\n1996\t\n1997\t**Context propagation.** The trace ID from `worker.session` is recorded in the file-sink event envelope as a new optional field `trace_id`, enabling correlation between the JSONL file sink and the OTel backend without ambiguity.\n1998\t\n1999\t### Metrics\n2000\t\n2001\tMetrics are emitted via the OTel Meter API, one `Meter` per worker. All metrics are prefixed `needle.*`.\n2002\t\n2003\t| Metric | Instrument | Unit | Attributes | Description |\n2004\t|--------|-----------|------|------------|-------------|\n2005\t| `needle.workers.active` | UpDownCounter | `{worker}` | — | Current live worker count (incremented on `worker.started`, decremented on `worker.stopped`) |\n2006\t| `needle.beads.claimed` | Counter | `{bead}` | `strand`, `priority` | Successful bead claims |\n2007\t| `needle.beads.completed` | Counter | `{bead}` | `outcome` | Bead terminal outcomes (one per `bead.outcome`) |\n2008\t| `model` | Output tokens produced |\n2014\t| `needle.cost.usd` | Counter | `USD` | `agent`, `model` | Estimated cost accumulator |\n2015\t| `needle.heartbeat.age` | Gauge (observable) | `s` | upstream.\n2022\t\n2023\t### Logs\n2024\t\n2025\tEvery NEEDLE telemetry event that isn't already represented as a span event is exported as an OTel LogRecord with:\n2026\t\n2027\t- `severity_number` / `severity_text`: `INFO` for normal events, `WARN` for `peer.stale` / `telemetry.*.dropped`, `ERROR` for `worker.errored` / `bead.claim.failed` / `agent.timeout`.\n2028\t- `body`: the existing event `data` object.\n2029\t- `attributes`: flattened from the event envelope (`event_type`, `bead_id`, `workspace`, etc.).\n2030\t- `trace_id` / `span_id`: linked to the enclosing `bead.lifecycle` or `worker.session` span where applicable.\n2031\t\n2032\tEvents that ARE spans (e.g., `bead.claim.attempted` → a span, not a log) do not double-export as logs.\n2033\t\n2034\t### Span Events vs. Logs\n2035\t\n2036\tIntra-span state changes (e.g., `agent.executing` heartbeats, `heartbeat.emitted`) are recorded as OTel **span events** on the nearest enclosing span, not as separate logs. This keeps the signal count manageable and makes timelines in Tempo/Jaeger readable.\n2037\t\n2038\t## Token and Cost Tracking\n2039\t\n2040\t### Token Extraction\n2041\t\n2042\tNEEDLE attempts to extract token usage from agent output. This is agent-specific and best-effort:\n2043\t\n2044\t| Agent | Extraction Method |\n2045\t|-------|-------------------|\n2046\t| Claude Code | Parse `--output-format json` for `usage.input_tokens`, `usage.output_tokens` |\n2047\t| OpenCode | Parse structured output (TBD) |\n2048\t| Codex CLI | Parse structured output (TBD) |\n2049\t| Aider | Parse cost summary line from stderr |\n2050\t| Generic | No extraction; record elapsed time only |\n2051\t\n2052\tIf token extraction fails, the event is still emitted with `null` token fields. Missing tokens are not an error.\n2053\t\n2054\t### Cost Estimation\n2055\t\n2056\tCost is estimated from tokens using configurable per-model pricing:\n2057\t\n2058\t```yaml\n2059\tpricing:\n2060\t  claude-sonnet:\n2061\t    input_per_million: 3.00\n2062\t    output_per_million: 15.00\n2063\t  claude-opus:\n2064\t    input_per_million: 15.00\n2065\t    output_per_million: 75.00\n2066\t  gpt-4:\n2067\t    input_per_million: 30.00\n2068\t    output_per_million: 60.00\n2069\t```\n2070\t\n2071\tCost is **estimated**, never authoritative. It is recorded in telemetry for trend analysis, not for billing.\n2072\t\n2073\t## Querying Telemetry\n2074\t\n2075\tNEEDLE includes built-in telemetry queries via the CLI:\n2076\t\n2077\t```bash\n2078\t# Summary of today's work\n2079\tneedle status\n2080\t\n2081\t# Per-worker breakdown\n2082\tneedle status --by-worker\n2083\t\n2084\t# Cost summary\n2085\tneedle status --cost --since 2026-03-20\n2086\t\n2087\t# Event stream (tail -f equivalent)\n2088\tneedle logs --follow\n2089\t\n2090\t# Filter by event type\n2091\tneedle logs --filter \"bead.claim.*\" --since 1h\n2092\t\n2093\t# Export for external analysis\n2094\tneedle logs --format jsonl --since 24h > export.jsonl\n2095\t```\n2096\t\n2097\t---\n2098\t\n2099\t# Self-Healing\n2100\t\n2101\tNEEDLE workers must detect and recover from failures without human intervention. This section specifies the failure modes, detection mechanisms, and recovery procedures.\n2102\t\n2103\t## Failure Taxonomy\n2104\t\n2105\t| Failure | Scope | Detection | Recovery |\n2106\t|---------|-------|-----------|----------|\n2107\t| Worker crash | Worker | Heartbeat TTL expiry | Peer cleanup via Mend |\n2108\t| Worker stuck | Worker | Heartbeat stale + PID alive | Alert via Knot |\n2109\t| Agent hang | Bead | Execution timeout | Kill process, release bead |\n2110\t| Stale claim | Bead | in_progress + no heartbeat | Mend releases bead |\n2111\t| Orphaned lock | Workspace | Lock file age > TTL | Mend removes lock |\n2112\t| Database corruption | Workspace | `br doctor` detects | Auto-repair from JSONL |\n2113\t| Stale dependency | Bead | Closed bead still blocks open bead | Mend cleans dependency |\n2114\t| Disk full | System | Write failure | Emit alert, graceful stop |\n2115\t| Bead store unreachable | System | `br` command fails | Retry with backoff, then stop |\n2116\t\n2117\t## Heartbeat-Based Detection\n2118\t\n2119\t```\n2120\tWorker A (alive)          Worker B (alive)         Worker C (crashed)\n2121\t┌──────────────┐         ┌──────────────┐         ┌──────────────┐\n2122\t│ heartbeat:   │         │ heartbeat:   │         │ heartbeat:   │\n2123\t│ 15:30:00     │         │ 15:30:10     │         │ 15:20:00     │ ← stale\n2124\t│ state: EXEC  │         │ state: SEL   │         │ state: EXEC  │\n2125\t│ bead: nd-a3f │         │ bead: null   │         │ bead: nd-x7y │ ← orphaned claim\n2126\t└──────────────┘         └──────────────┘         └──────────────┘\n2127\t\n2128\tWorker B runs Mend strand:\n2129\t  1. Reads all heartbeat files\n2130\t  2. Detects C's heartbeat is stale (10 min old, TTL is 5 min)\n2131\t  3. Checks PID: dead\n2132\t  4. Releases nd-x7y: br update nd-x7y --status open --unassign\n2133\t  5. Removes C's heartbeat file\n2134\t  6. Deregisters C from worker registry\n2135\t  7. Emits peer.crashed telemetry\n2136\t```\n2137\t\n2138\t### Detection Parameters\n2139\t\n2140\t| Parameter | Default | Description |\n2141\t|-----------|---------|-------------|\n2142\t| `heartbeat_interval` | 30s | How often a worker writes its heartbeat |\n2143\t| `heartbeat_ttl` | 5min | How long before a heartbeat is considered stale |\n2144\t| `peer_check_interval` | 60s | How often Mend checks peer heartbeats |\n2145\t\n2146\t**Relationship:** `heartbeat_ttl` should be at least `3 × heartbeat_interval` to tolerate transient delays.\n2147\t\n2148\t### Stuck vs. Crashed\n2149\t\n2150\t| Signal | Diagnosis | Action |\n2151\t|--------|-----------|--------|\n2152\t| Stale heartbeat + PID dead | **Crashed.** Worker terminated unexpectedly. | Release claim, clean up, emit `peer.crashed` |\n2153\t| Stale heartbeat + PID alive | **Stuck.** Worker is hung (deadlock, infinite loop, blocked I/O). | Emit `peer.stale` warning. Do NOT kill — may be legitimately slow. Alert via Knot after threshold. |\n2154\t| Fresh heartbeat + PID alive | **Healthy.** Normal operation. | No action. |\n2155\t\n2156\t**NEEDLE does not auto-kill stuck workers.** A stuck worker with a live PID may be executing a legitimately slow agent. Killing it would interrupt work. Instead, NEEDLE alerts via Knot and lets the human decide.\n2157\t\n2158\t## Database Recovery\n2159\t\n2160\tbeads_rust uses SQLite with a known corruption issue (FrankenSQLite, upstream #171). NEEDLE must handle this.\n2161\t\n2162\t### Recovery Procedure\n2163\t\n2164\t```\n2165\tCorruption detected\n2166\t       │\n2167\t       ▼\n2168\t  Run br doctor --repair\n2169\t       │\n2170\t       ├── Success ──► Resume operation, emit health.db_repaired\n2171\t       │\n2172\t       └── Failure ──► Full rebuild:\n2173\t                          1. rm .beads/beads.db\n2174\t                          2. br sync --import\n2175\t                          3. Verify: br doctor\n2176\t                          │\n2177\t                          ├── Success ──► Resume, emit health.db_rebuilt\n2178\t                          │\n2179\t                          └── Failure ──► ERRORED state (JSONL itself may be corrupt)\n2180\t```\n2181\t\n2182\t**Key insight from `docs/notes/mitosis-explosion-postmortem.md`:** The JSONL file is always the authoritative data source. It is append-only and immune to SQLite corruption. Recovery always rebuilds from JSONL.\n2183\t\n2184\t### Proactive Health Checks\n2185\t\n2186\tThe Mend strand runs `br doctor` (without `--repair`) periodically:\n2187\t- After every N beads processed (configurable, default: 50)\n2188\t- On every Mend strand evaluation\n2189\t- If doctor reports warnings, escalate to `--repair` immediately rather than waiting for failure\n2190\t\n2191\t## Stale Claim Recovery\n2192\t\n2193\t```\n2194\tMend strand evaluates:\n2195\t  1. Query beads with status=in_progress\n2196\t  2. For each:\n2197\t     a. Read assigned worker ID from bead\n2198\t     b. Check worker's heartbeat file\n2199\t     c. If heartbeat is stale AND PID is dead:\n2200\t        - br update <bead_id> --status open --unassign\n2201\t        - Emit bead.released telemetry (reason: stale_claim)\n2202\t     d. If heartbeat is stale AND PID is alive:\n2203\t        - Emit peer.stale warning (do not release — worker may be slow)\n2204\t     e. If heartbeat is fresh:\n2205\t        - Normal operation, skip\n2206\t```\n2207\t\n2208\tA claimed bead is only released if the owning worker is **confirmed dead** (stale heartbeat AND dead PID). If the PID is alive, the bead is not released, even if the heartbeat is stale.\n2209\t\n2210\t## Lock File Recovery\n2211\t\n2212\tMend strand checks lock file age:\n2213\t1. Read lock files in `/tmp/needle-claim-*.lock`\n2214\t2. If file modification time > `lock_ttl` (default: 10 minutes):\n2215\t   - Attempt to acquire flock (non-blocking)\n2216\t   - If acquired: no one holds it, delete the file, release flock\n2217\t   - If not acquired: someone is actively holding it, skip\n2218\t\n2219\t## Dependency Link Recovery\n2220\t\n2221\tMend strand checks for stale dependencies:\n2222\t1. Query beads with status `open` that have blockers\n2223\t2. For each blocker, check if the blocking bead is closed\n2224\t3. If blocker is closed, remove the dependency link\n2225\t4. Emit `bead.dependency.cleaned` telemetry\n2226\t\n2227\tThis is a necessary compensating mechanism because `br` does not automatically resolve dependency links on bead closure (documented in `docs/notes/bead-lifecycle-bugs.md`).\n2228\t\n2229\t## Graceful Degradation\n2230\t\n2231\tWhen subsystems fail, NEEDLE degrades gracefully rather than crashing:\n2232\t\n2233\t| Subsystem Failure | Degradation |\n2234\t|-------------------|-------------|\n2235\t| Telemetry file sink unwritable | Buffer events in memory, retry. If buffer full, drop events. Worker continues. |\n2236\t| Heartbeat file unwritable | Log error. Worker continues but cannot be monitored by peers. If persistent, ERRORED. |\n2237\t| Worker registry unwritable | Log error. Worker continues but invisible to `needle list`. |\n2238\t| Database corrupt | Auto-repair. If repair fails, ERRORED for that workspace only. |\n2239\t| Single workspace unreachable | Skip workspace in Explore, continue with others. |\n2240\t| Config file unreadable mid-session | Use cached config from boot. Emit warning. |\n2241\t\n2242\t## Self-Modification and Release Channels\n2243\t\n2244\tNEEDLE workers are allowed to modify NEEDLE itself. The v1 failures (see `docs/notes/self-modification-risks.md`) were not caused by self-modification as a concept — they were caused by untested changes deploying directly to the running fleet. The solution is not to ban self-modification but to gate promotion through release channels with canary testing.\n2245\t\n2246\t### Release Channels\n2247\t\n2248\t```\n2249\t:testing ──► :stable ──► fleet hot-reload\n2250\t                │\n2251\t                └── rollback to previous :stable on failure\n2252\t```\n2253\t\n2254\tThree channels:\n2255\t\n2256\t| Channel | Purpose | Who writes | Who reads |\n2257\t|---------|---------|------------|-----------|\n2258\t| `:testing` | Newly built binary, not yet validated | Worker that built it | Canary test harness only |\n2259\t| `:stable` | Validated binary, approved for fleet use | Promotion pipeline (after canary passes) | Running fleet via hot-reload |\n2260\t| `:latest` | Alias for the most recent `:stable` | Automatic on promotion | `needle upgrade` default target |\n2261\t\n2262\t### Canary Testing Pipeline\n2263\t\n2264\tWhen a worker modifies NEEDLE's source and builds a new binary:\n2265\t\n2266\t```\n2267\tWorker builds new binary\n2268\t       │\n2269\t       ▼\n2270\t  Install as :testing\n2271\t  (~/.needle/bin/needle-testing)\n2272\t       │\n2273\t       ▼\n2274\t  Run canary test suite:\n2275\t    1. Launch :testing binary with test .beads/ directory\n2276\t    2. Test beads have defined inputs and expected outcomes\n2277\t    3. :testing processes beads in isolation\n2278\t    4. Compare actual outcomes against expected\n2279\t       │\n2280\t       ├── All pass → Promote :testing to :stable\n2281\t       │                 │\n2282\t       │                 ▼\n2283\t       │              Fleet detects new :stable\n2284\t       │              Workers hot-reload on next bead boundary\n2285\t       │\n2286\t       └── Any fail → Reject :testing\n2287\t                        │\n2288\t                        ▼\n2289\t                     Mark bead as failed\n2290\t                     :stable remains unchanged\n2291\t                     Fleet continues on previous :stable\n2292\t                     Emit canary.failed telemetry\n2293\t```\n2294\t\n2295\t### Canary Test Suite\n2296\t\n2297\tThe canary suite is a set of test beads with known-good outcomes stored in a dedicated test workspace:\n2298\t\n2299\t```\n2300\t~/.needle/canary/\n2301\t├── .beads/                    # test bead store\n2302\t│   ├── issues.jsonl\n2303\t│   └── beads.db\n2304\t├── test-workspace/            # mock workspace with source files\n2305\t│   ├── src/\n2306\t│   │   └── hello.py           # simple file for beads to modify\n2307\t│   └── .beads/\n2308\t└── expected/                  # expected outcomes per bead\n2309\t    ├── bead-001.expected.json # { \"exit_code\": 0, \"bead_closed\": true }\n2310\t    ├── bead-002.expected.json # { \"exit_code\": 0, \"files_modified\": [\"src/hello.py\"] }\n2311\t    └── bead-003.expected.json # { \"exit_code\": 1, \"bead_closed\": false }\n2312\t```\n2313\t\n2314\tTest beads cover:\n2315\t- **Happy path:** Simple bead that should succeed and close\n2316\t- **Failure path:** Bead that should fail (tests outcome handling)\n2317\t- **Timeout path:** Bead with intentionally slow agent (tests timeout enforcement)\n2318\t- **State machine integrity:** Verify telemetry events match expected state transitions\n2319\t- **Mitosis:** Multi-task bead that should split on failure\n2320\t\n2321\t### Hot-Reload Protocol\n2322\t\n2323\tRunning workers check for a new `:stable` binary between bead processing cycles (after LOGGING, before SELECTING):\n2324\t\n2325\t1. Compare current binary hash against `:stable` binary hash\n2326\t2. If different:\n2327\t   a. Emit `worker.upgrade.detected` telemetry\n2328\t   b. Complete current bead cycle (never interrupt mid-execution)\n2329\t   c. Re-exec with the new binary: `exec ~/.needle/bin/needle-stable run --resume`\n2330\t   d. New binary picks up worker state from heartbeat file and registry\n2331\t3. If same: continue normally\n2332\t\n2333\t**`--resume` flag:** Tells the new binary to inherit the worker's identity (ID, session, tmux) rather than creating a new session. The worker continues from the SELECTING state with a fresh binary.\n2334\t\n2335\t### Rollback\n2336\t\n2337\tIf a promoted `:stable` causes failures in the fleet:\n2338\t\n2339\t1. Fleet workers emit `worker.errored` or repeated `outcome.failure` telemetry\n2340\t2. Human (or automated watchdog) runs: `needle rollback`\n2341\t3. Rollback restores the previous `:stable` from backup (`~/.needle/bin/needle-stable.prev`)\n2342\t4. Workers hot-reload to the rolled-back binary on next cycle\n2343\t\n2344\tRollback is always available because promotion preserves the previous `:stable` as a backup.\n2345\t\n2346\t### Binary Paths\n2347\t\n2348\t```\n2349\t~/.needle/bin/\n2350\t├── needle-testing             # candidate under canary evaluation\n2351\t├── needle-stable              # current fleet binary\n2352\t├── needle-stable.prev         # previous stable (rollback target)\n2353\t└── needle                     # symlink → needle-stable\n2354\t```\n2355\t\n2356\t### Configuration\n2357\t\n2358\t```yaml\n2359\tself_modification:\n2360\t  enabled: true                     # allow workers to process NEEDLE beads\n2361\t  canary_workspace: ~/.needle/canary  # test workspace with known-good beads\n2362\t  auto_promote: true                # promote to :stable automatically if canary passes\n2363\t  hot_reload: true                  # fleet hot-reloads from :stable between beads\n2364\t```\n2365\t\n2366\t### Telemetry\n2367\t\n2368\t| Event Type | Emitted When | Data Fields |\n2369\t|------------|-------------|-------------|\n2370\t| `canary.started` | `rolled_back_hash`, `restored_hash` OTLP Sink (optional)\n\nExports telemetry as OpenTelemetry signals (traces, metrics, logs) over OTLP to any compliant collector (OpenTelemetry Collector, Jaeger, Tempo, Grafana Alloy, Honeycomb, Datadog, etc.). This is the canonical integration point for FABRIC and any downstream observability plane.\n\n```yaml\ntelemetry:\n  otlp:\n    enabled: true\n    endpoint: \"http://otel-collector.tailnet:4317\"    # gRPC default; use 4318 for HTTP\n    protocol: grpc                                     # grpc | http/protobuf\n    headers:\n      authorization: \"Bearer ${OTEL_TOKEN}\"            # env interpolation\n    timeout_ms: 5000\n    compression: gzip                                  # none | gzip\n    tls:\n      insecure: false\n      ca_file: \"\"\n    signals:\n      traces: true\n      metrics: true\n      logs: true\n    resource_attributes:\n      deployment.environment: \"production\"\n      service.namespace: \"needle-fleet\"\n```\n\nDesign:\n\n- **Non-blocking.** Uses a batch span/log/metric processor. If the collector is unreachable, events are buffered up to a bounded queue, then dropped (same policy as file sink). Drops emit a `telemetry.otlp.dropped` event to the file sink (never recursively to OTLP).\n- **Additive.** The file sink is authoritative. OTLP is an export, not a replacement. If OTLP is disabled or misconfigured, NEEDLE behaves identically to a file-sink-only deployment.\n- **Stdlib deps.** Rust crates: `opentelemetry`, `opentelemetry_sdk`, `opentelemetry-otlp`, `opentelemetry-semantic-conventions`. All support OTLP/gRPC and OTLP/HTTP.\n- **W3C trace context.** Trace and span IDs are generated per the W3C Trace Context spec so they interop with any OTel backend.\n- **Graceful shutdown.** On `worker.stopped`, the exporter is flushed with a deadline before process exit. Failure to flush is logged but never blocks shutdown.\n\n## OpenTelemetry Semantic Mapping\n\nNEEDLE's existing event catalog maps cleanly to OpenTelemetry's three signal types. This mapping is **normative** — the OTLP sink implementation must conform to it so dashboards and alerts remain stable across NEEDLE versions.\n\n### Resource Attributes\n\nEvery exported signal carries these resource attributes (per OTel semantic conventions):\n\n| Attribute | Value | Source |\n|-----------|-------|--------|\n| `service.name` | `\"needle\"` | Constant |\n| `service.version` | build version | `env!(\"CARGO_PKG_VERSION\")` |\n| `service.instance.id` | `<worker_id>` | e.g., `needle-claude-anthropic-sonnet-alpha` |\n| `service.namespace` | `\"needle-fleet\"` (default, configurable) | Config |\n| `deployment.environment` | e.g., `\"production\"` | Config |\n| `host.name` | hostname | OS |\n| `process.pid` | worker PID | OS |\n| `needle.agent` | e.g., `\"claude-anthropic-sonnet\"` | Worker config |\n| `needle.model` | e.g., `\"claude-sonnet-4-6\"` | Worker config |\n| `needle.session_id` | session ID | Per-boot random |\n| `needle.workspace` | workspace path | Worker config |\n\n### Traces\n\nThe NEEDLE state machine is naturally hierarchical, which maps directly to OTel spans.\n\n```\nworker.session                                          (root span, lifetime = worker process)\n├── strand.pluck                                        (one per strand evaluation)\n│   └── bead.lifecycle                                  (one per claimed bead)\n│       ├── bead.claim                                  (ATOMIC phase)\n│       ├── bead.prompt_build\n│       ├── agent.dispatch                              (DISPATCHING + EXECUTING)\n│       │   └── agent.execution                         (process alive; span.ok on exit 0)\n│       └── bead.outcome                                (HANDLING)\n│           └── bead.mitosis?                           (optional, if outcome = failure)\n├── strand.mend\n├── strand.explore\n├── strand.weave\n├── strand.unravel\n├── strand.pulse\n└── strand.knot                                         (terminal backoff / exhaustion)\n```\n\nSpan naming follows OpenTelemetry conventions: lowercase dotted, verb-form where appropriate.\n\n**Span attributes** follow OTel semantic conventions where applicable, plus a `needle.*` namespace:\n\n| Span | Key Attributes |\n|------|----------------|\n| `worker.session` | `needle.beads_processed`, `needle.uptime_seconds`, `needle.exit_reason` |\n| `strand.*` | `needle.strand.name`, `needle.strand.result`, `needle.strand.duration_ms` |\n| `bead.lifecycle` | `needle.bead.id`, `needle.bead.priority`, `needle.bead.title_hash`, `needle.bead.outcome` |\n| `bead.claim` | `needle.claim.retry_number`, `needle.claim.result` (`succeeded` / `race_lost` / `failed`) |\n| `agent.dispatch` | `gen_ai.system` (e.g., `anthropic`), `gen_ai.request.model`, `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens`, `gen_ai.usage.output_tokens`, `needle.agent.pid`, `needle.agent.exit_code` |\n| `bead.outcome` | `needle.outcome` (`success` / `failure` / `timeout` / `crash` / `agent_not_found` / `interrupted`), `needle.outcome.action` |\n\n**GenAI semantic conventions.** The `agent.dispatch` span uses OTel's `gen_ai.*` conventions so NEEDLE's token/cost data shows up in GenAI dashboards out-of-the-box (Grafana GenAI app, Langfuse, Honeycomb AI, etc.).\n\n**Span status.** Success outcomes set `Status::Ok`. All other outcomes set `Status::Error` with a description matching the `needle.outcome` value. This makes error-rate SLOs trivial.\n\n**Context propagation.** The trace ID from `worker.session` is recorded in the file-sink event envelope as a new optional field `trace_id`, enabling correlation between the JSONL file sink and the OTel backend without ambiguity.\n\n### Metrics\n\nMetrics are emitted via the OTel Meter API, one `Meter` per worker. All metrics are prefixed `needle.*`.\n\n| Metric | Instrument | Unit | Attributes | Description |\n|--------|-----------|------|------------|-------------|\n| `needle.workers.active` | UpDownCounter | `{worker}` | — | Current live worker count (incremented on `worker.started`, decremented on `worker.stopped`) |\n| `needle.beads.claimed` | Counter | `{bead}` | `strand`, `priority` | Successful bead claims |\n| `needle.beads.completed` | Counter | `{bead}` | `outcome` | Bead terminal outcomes (one per `bead.outcome`) |\n| `needle.beads.duration` | Histogram | `ms` | `outcome` | End-to-end bead lifecycle time |\n| `needle.claim.attempts` | Counter | `{attempt}` | `result` (`succeeded`/`race_lost`/`failed`) | Claim attempts |\n| `needle.strand.duration` | Histogram | `ms` | `strand`, `result` | Strand evaluation time |\n| `needle.agent.duration` | Histogram | `ms` | `agent`, `model`, `exit_code` | Agent process runtime |\n| `needle.agent.tokens.input` | Counter | `{token}` | `agent`, `model` | Input tokens consumed |\n| `needle.agent.tokens.output` | Counter | `{token}` | `agent`, `model` | Output tokens produced |\n| `needle.cost.usd` | Counter | `USD` | `agent`, `model` | Estimated cost accumulator |\n| `needle.heartbeat.age` | Gauge (observable) | `s` | `worker_id` | Seconds since last heartbeat emitted by this worker |\n| `needle.peers.stale` | UpDownCounter | `{peer}` | — | Currently-stale peers observed by this worker |\n| `needle.queue.depth` | Gauge (observable) | `{bead}` | `workspace`, `priority` | Open beads visible to this worker (sampled at strand evaluation) |\n| `needle.mitosis.children_created` | Counter | `{bead}` | `parent_id` | Mitosis child creations |\n| `needle.outcome.rate` | derived | — | — | Computed in the backend as `needle.beads.completed{outcome=\"success\"} / needle.beads.completed` |\n\nMetric aggregation temporality is **delta** (standard OTel default); backends that require cumulative (Prometheus via prometheusreceiver) convert upstream.\n\n### Logs\n\nEvery NEEDLE telemetry event that isn't already represented as a span event is exported as an OTel LogRecord with:\n\n- `severity_number` / `severity_text`: `INFO` for normal events, `WARN` for `peer.stale` / `telemetry.*.dropped`, `ERROR` for `worker.errored` / `bead.claim.failed` / `agent.timeout`.\n- `body`: the existing event `data` object.\n- `attributes`: flattened from the event envelope (`event_type`, `bead_id`, `workspace`, etc.).\n- `trace_id` / `span_id`: linked to the enclosing `bead.lifecycle` or `worker.session` span where applicable.\n\nEvents that ARE spans (e.g., `bead.claim.attempted` → a span, not a log) do not double-export as logs.\n\n### Span Events vs. Logs\n\nIntra-span state changes (e.g., `agent.executing` heartbeats, `heartbeat.emitted`) are recorded as OTel **span events** on the nearest enclosing span, not as separate logs. This keeps the signal count manageable and makes timelines in Tempo/Jaeger readable.\n\n## Token and Cost Tracking\n\n### Token Extraction\n\nNEEDLE attempts to extract token usage from agent output. This is agent-specific and best-effort:\n\n| Agent | Extraction Method |\n|-------|-------------------|\n| Claude Code | Parse `--output-format json` for `usage.input_tokens`, `usage.output_tokens` |\n| OpenCode | Parse structured output (TBD) |\n| Codex CLI | Parse structured output (TBD) |\n| Aider | Parse cost summary line from stderr |\n| Generic | No extraction; record elapsed time only |\n\nIf token extraction fails, the event is still emitted with `null` token fields. Missing tokens are not an error.\n\n### Cost Estimation\n\nCost is estimated from tokens using configurable per-model pricing:\n\n```yaml\npricing:\n  claude-sonnet:\n    input_per_million: 3.00\n    output_per_million: 15.00\n  claude-opus:\n    input_per_million: 15.00\n    output_per_million: 75.00\n  gpt-4:\n    input_per_million: 30.00\n    output_per_million: 60.00\n```\n\nCost is **estimated**, never authoritative. It is recorded in telemetry for trend analysis, not for billing.\n\n## Querying Telemetry\n\nNEEDLE includes built-in telemetry queries via the CLI:\n\n```bash\n# Summary of today's work\nneedle status\n\n# Per-worker breakdown\nneedle status --by-worker\n\n# Cost summary\nneedle status --cost --since 2026-03-20\n\n# Event stream (tail -f equivalent)\nneedle logs --follow\n\n# Filter by event type\nneedle logs --filter \"bead.claim.*\" --since 1h\n\n# Export for external analysis\nneedle logs --format jsonl --since 24h > export.jsonl\n```\n\n---\n\n# Self-Healing\n\nNEEDLE workers must detect and recover from failures without human intervention. This section specifies the failure modes, detection mechanisms, and recovery procedures.\n\n## Failure Taxonomy\n\n| Failure | Scope | Detection | Recovery |\n|---------|-------|-----------|----------|\n| Worker crash | Worker | Heartbeat TTL expiry | Peer cleanup via Mend |\n| Worker stuck | Worker | Heartbeat stale + PID alive | Alert via Knot |\n| Agent hang | Bead | Execution timeout | Kill process, release bead |\n| Stale claim | Bead | in_progress + no heartbeat | Mend releases bead |\n| Orphaned lock | Workspace | Lock file age > TTL | Mend removes lock |\n| Database corruption | Workspace | `br doctor` detects | Auto-repair from JSONL |\n| Stale dependency | Bead | Closed bead still blocks open bead | Mend cleans dependency |\n| Disk full | System | Write failure | Emit alert, graceful stop |\n| Bead store unreachable | System | `br` command fails | Retry with backoff, then stop |\n\n## Heartbeat-Based Detection\n\n```\nWorker A (alive)          Worker B (alive)         Worker C (crashed)\n┌──────────────┐         ┌──────────────┐         ┌──────────────┐\n│ heartbeat:   │         │ heartbeat:   │         │ heartbeat:   │\n│ 15:30:00     │         │ 15:30:10     │         │ 15:20:00     │ ← stale\n│ state: EXEC  │         │ state: SEL   │         │ state: EXEC  │\n│ bead: nd-a3f │         │ bead: null   │         │ bead: nd-x7y │ ← orphaned claim\n└──────────────┘         └──────────────┘         └──────────────┘\n\nWorker B runs Mend strand:\n  1. Reads all heartbeat files\n  2. Detects C's heartbeat is stale (10 min old, TTL is 5 min)\n  3. Checks PID: dead\n  4. Releases nd-x7y: br update nd-x7y --status open --unassign\n  5. Removes C's heartbeat file\n  6. Deregisters C from worker registry\n  7. Emits peer.crashed telemetry\n```\n\n### Detection Parameters\n\n| Parameter | Default | Description |\n|-----------|---------|-------------|\n| `heartbeat_interval` | 30s | How often a worker writes its heartbeat |\n| `heartbeat_ttl` | 5min | How long before a heartbeat is considered stale |\n| `peer_check_interval` | 60s | How often Mend checks peer heartbeats |\n\n**Relationship:** `heartbeat_ttl` should be at least `3 × heartbeat_interval` to tolerate transient delays.\n\n### Stuck vs. Crashed\n\n| Signal | Diagnosis | Action |\n|--------|-----------|--------|\n| Stale heartbeat + PID dead | **Crashed.** Worker terminated unexpectedly. | Release claim, clean up, emit `peer.crashed` |\n| Stale heartbeat + PID alive | **Stuck.** Worker is hung (deadlock, infinite loop, blocked I/O). | Emit `peer.stale` warning. Do NOT kill — may be legitimately slow. Alert via Knot after threshold. |\n| Fresh heartbeat + PID alive | **Healthy.** Normal operation. | No action. |\n\n**NEEDLE does not auto-kill stuck workers.** A stuck worker with a live PID may be executing a legitimately slow agent. Killing it would interrupt work. Instead, NEEDLE alerts via Knot and lets the human decide.\n\n## Database Recovery\n\nbeads_rust uses SQLite with a known corruption issue (FrankenSQLite, upstream #171). NEEDLE must handle this.\n\n### Recovery Procedure\n\n```\nCorruption detected\n       │\n       ▼\n  Run br doctor --repair\n       │\n       ├── Success ──► Resume operation, emit health.db_repaired\n       │\n       └── Failure ──► Full rebuild:\n                          1. rm .beads/beads.db\n                          2. br sync --import\n                          3. Verify: br doctor\n                          │\n                          ├── Success ──► Resume, emit health.db_rebuilt\n                          │\n                          └── Failure ──► ERRORED state (JSONL itself may be corrupt)\n```\n\n**Key insight from `docs/notes/mitosis-explosion-postmortem.md`:** The JSONL file is always the authoritative data source. It is append-only and immune to SQLite corruption. Recovery always rebuilds from JSONL.\n\n### Proactive Health Checks\n\nThe Mend strand runs `br doctor` (without `--repair`) periodically:\n- After every N beads processed (configurable, default: 50)\n- On every Mend strand evaluation\n- If doctor reports warnings, escalate to `--repair` immediately rather than waiting for failure\n\n## Stale Claim Recovery\n\n```\nMend strand evaluates:\n  1. Query beads with status=in_progress\n  2. For each:\n     a. Read assigned worker ID from bead\n     b. Check worker's heartbeat file\n     c. If heartbeat is stale AND PID is dead:\n        - br update <bead_id> --status open --unassign\n        - Emit bead.released telemetry (reason: stale_claim)\n     d. If heartbeat is stale AND PID is alive:\n        - Emit peer.stale warning (do not release — worker may be slow)\n     e. If heartbeat is fresh:\n        - Normal operation, skip\n```\n\nA claimed bead is only released if the owning worker is **confirmed dead** (stale heartbeat AND dead PID). If the PID is alive, the bead is not released, even if the heartbeat is stale.\n\n## Lock File Recovery\n\nMend strand checks lock file age:\n1. Read lock files in `/tmp/needle-claim-*.lock`\n2. If file modification time > `lock_ttl` (default: 10 minutes):\n   - Attempt to acquire flock (non-blocking)\n   - If acquired: no one holds it, delete the file, release flock\n   - If not acquired: someone is actively holding it, skip\n\n## Dependency Link Recovery\n\nMend strand checks for stale dependencies:\n1. Query beads with status `open` that have blockers\n2. For each blocker, check if the blocking bead is closed\n3. If blocker is closed, remove the dependency link\n4. Emit `bead.dependency.cleaned` telemetry\n\nThis is a necessary compensating mechanism because `br` does not automatically resolve dependency links on bead closure (documented in `docs/notes/bead-lifecycle-bugs.md`).\n\n## Graceful Degradation\n\nWhen subsystems fail, NEEDLE degrades gracefully rather than crashing:\n\n| Subsystem Failure | Degradation |\n|-------------------|-------------|\n| Telemetry file sink unwritable | Buffer events in memory, retry. If buffer full, drop events. Worker continues. |\n| Heartbeat file unwritable | Log error. Worker continues but cannot be monitored by peers. If persistent, ERRORED. |\n| Worker registry unwritable | Log error. Worker continues but invisible to `needle list`. |\n| Database corrupt | Auto-repair. If repair fails, ERRORED for that workspace only. |\n| Single workspace unreachable | Skip workspace in Explore, continue with others. |\n| Config file unreadable mid-session | Use cached config from boot. Emit warning. |\n\n## Self-Modification and Release Channels\n\nNEEDLE workers are allowed to modify NEEDLE itself. The v1 failures (see `docs/notes/self-modification-risks.md`) were not caused by self-modification as a concept — they were caused by untested changes deploying directly to the running fleet. The solution is not to ban self-modification but to gate promotion through release channels with canary testing.\n\n### Release Channels\n\n```\n:testing ──► :stable ──► fleet hot-reload\n                │\n                └── rollback to previous :stable on failure\n```\n\nThree channels:\n\n| Channel | Purpose | Who writes | Who reads |\n|---------|---------|------------|-----------|\n| `:testing` | Newly built binary, not yet validated | Worker that built it | Canary test harness only |\n| `:stable` | Validated binary, approved for fleet use | Promotion pipeline (after canary passes) | Running fleet via hot-reload |\n| `:latest` | Alias for the most recent `:stable` | Automatic on promotion | `needle upgrade` default target |\n\n### Canary Testing Pipeline\n\nWhen a worker modifies NEEDLE's source and builds a new binary:\n\n```\nWorker builds new binary\n       │\n       ▼\n  Install as :testing\n  (~/.needle/bin/needle-testing)\n       │\n       ▼\n  Run canary test suite:\n    1. Launch :testing binary with test .beads/ directory\n    2. Test beads have defined inputs and expected outcomes\n    3. :testing processes beads in isolation\n    4. Compare actual outcomes against expected\n       │\n       ├── All pass → Promote :testing to :stable\n       │                 │\n       │                 ▼\n       │              Fleet detects new :stable\n       │              Workers hot-reload on next bead boundary\n       │\n       └── Any fail → Reject :testing\n                        │\n                        ▼\n                     Mark bead as failed\n                     :stable remains unchanged\n                     Fleet continues on previous :stable\n                     Emit canary.failed telemetry\n```\n\n### Canary Test Suite\n\nThe canary suite is a set of test beads with known-good outcomes stored in a dedicated test workspace:\n\n```\n~/.needle/canary/\n├── .beads/                    # test bead store\n│   ├── issues.jsonl\n│   └── beads.db\n├── test-workspace/            # mock workspace with source files\n│   ├── src/\n│   │   └── hello.py           # simple file for beads to modify\n│   └── .beads/\n└── expected/                  # expected outcomes per bead\n    ├── bead-001.expected.json # { \"exit_code\": 0, \"bead_closed\": true }\n    ├── bead-002.expected.json # { \"exit_code\": 0, \"files_modified\": [\"src/hello.py\"] }\n    └── bead-003.expected.json # { \"exit_code\": 1, \"bead_closed\": false }\n```\n\nTest beads cover:\n- **Happy path:** Simple bead that should succeed and close\n- **Failure path:** Bead that should fail (tests outcome handling)\n- **Timeout path:** Bead with intentionally slow agent (tests timeout enforcement)\n- **State machine integrity:** Verify telemetry events match expected state transitions\n- **Mitosis:** Multi-task bead that should split on failure\n\n### Hot-Reload Protocol\n\nRunning workers check for a new `:stable` binary between bead processing cycles (after LOGGING, before SELECTING):\n\n1. Compare current binary hash against `:stable` binary hash\n2. If different:\n   a. Emit `worker.upgrade.detected` telemetry\n   b. Complete current bead cycle (never interrupt mid-execution)\n   c. Re-exec with the new binary: `exec ~/.needle/bin/needle-stable run --resume`\n   d. New binary picks up worker state from heartbeat file and registry\n3. If same: continue normally\n\n**`--resume` flag:** Tells the new binary to inherit the worker's identity (ID, session, tmux) rather than creating a new session. The worker continues from the SELECTING state with a fresh binary.\n\n### Rollback\n\nIf a promoted `:stable` causes failures in the fleet:\n\n1. Fleet workers emit `worker.errored` or repeated `outcome.failure` telemetry\n2. Human (or automated watchdog) runs: `needle rollback`\n3. Rollback restores the previous `:stable` from backup (`~/.needle/bin/needle-stable.prev`)\n4. Workers hot-reload to the rolled-back binary on next cycle\n\nRollback is always available because promotion preserves the previous `:stable` as a backup.\n\n### Binary Paths\n\n```\n~/.needle/bin/\n├── needle-testing             # candidate under canary evaluation\n├── needle-stable              # current fleet binary\n├── needle-stable.prev         # previous stable (rollback target)\n└── needle                     # symlink → needle-stable\n```\n\n### Configuration\n\n```yaml\nself_modification:\n  enabled: true                     # allow workers to process NEEDLE beads\n  canary_workspace: ~/.needle/canary  # test workspace with known-good beads\n  auto_promote: true                # promote to :stable automatically if canary passes\n  hot_reload: true                  # fleet hot-reloads from :stable between beads\n```\n\n### Telemetry\n\n| Event Type | Emitted When | Data Fields |\n|------------|-------------|-------------|\n| `canary.started` | Canary test suite begins | `testing_binary_hash`, `test_count` |\n| `canary.passed` | All canary tests passed | `testing_binary_hash`, `duration_ms` |\n| `canary.failed` | One or more canary tests failed | `testing_binary_hash`, `failures` (list) |\n| `promotion.completed` | :testing promoted to :stable | `old_hash`, `new_hash` |\n| `worker.upgrade.detected` | Worker sees new :stable | `old_hash`, `new_hash` |\n| `worker.upgrade.completed` | Worker re-exec'd with new binary | `new_hash` |\n| `rollback.completed` | :stable rolled back to previous | `rolled_back_hash`, `restored_hash` |\n","numLines":500,"startLine":1878,"totalLines":4089}}}

If present, it's a regex pattern - no conversion needed\n95\t/// 3. If absent, but * is present, it's a glob pattern - convert it\n96\tfn needs_glob_conversion(pattern: &str) -> bool {\n97\t    // First, check if it looks like a regex by looking for regex metacharacters.\n98\t    // The key indicator is .* which is \"any character\" in regex but not in glob.\n99\t    let has_regex_features = pattern.contains(|c| {\n100\t        matches!(\n101\t            c,\n102\t            '^' | '$' | '(' | ')' | '[' | ']' | '{' | '}' | '+' | '?' | '|' | '\\\\'\n103\t        )\n104\t    }) || pattern.contains(\".*\");\n105\t\n106\t    if has_regex_features {\n107\t        // Has clear regex features - treat as regex\n108\t        return false;\n109\t    }\n110\t\n111\t    // At this point, we have a simple pattern that might be glob or regex.\n112\t    // If it contains unescaped * (and we already ruled out other regex chars),\n113\t    // treat it as a glob pattern.\n114\t    let chars: Vec<char> = pattern.chars().collect();\n115\t    let mut i = 0;\n116\t\n117\t    while i < chars.len() {\n118\t        if chars[i] == '\\\\' && i + 1 < chars.len() {\n119\t            // Skip escaped character.\n120\t            i += 2;\n121\t            continue;\n122\t        }\n123\t        if chars[i] == '*' {\n124\t            return true;\n125\t        }\n126\t        i += 1;\n127\t    }\n128\t\n129\t    false\n130\t}\n131\t\n132\t/// Convert glob-style pattern to regex.\n133\t///\n134\t/// Rules:\n135\t/// - `*` alone → `.*` (match anything, catch-all)\n136\t/// - `*` in other contexts → `[^/]+` (match any single segment, no slashes)\n137\t/// - `**` → `.*` (match any characters including slashes, greedy)\n138\t/// - Escaped `\\*` and `\\*\\*` treated literally\n139\t/// - No implicit start anchor for glob patterns (unlike regex patterns)\n140\tfn convert_glob_to_regex(glob: &str) -> String {\n141\t    // Special case: * and ** should match anything (including empty).\n142\t    if glob == \"*\" || glob == \"**\" {\n143\t        return \"^.*$\".to_string();\n144\t    }\n145\t\n146\t    let mut result = String::new();\n147\t    let chars: Vec<char> = glob.chars().collect();\n148\t    let mut i = 0;\n149\t\n150\t    while i < chars.len() {\n151\t        match chars[i] {\n152\t            '\\\\' => {\n153\t                // Escaped character - pass through the backslash and the character.\n154\t                // This ensures that \\* in the glob becomes \\* in the regex (literal asterisk).\n155\t                if i + 1 < chars.len() {\n156\t                    result.push('\\\\');\n157\t                    result.push(chars[i + 1]);\n158\t                    i += 2;\n159\t                } else {\n160\t                    // Trailing backslash - treat literally.\n161\t                    result.push('\\\\');\n162\t                    i += 1;\n163\t                }\n164\t            }\n165\t            '*' => {\n166\t                // Check for **.\n167\t                if i + 1 < chars.len() && chars[i + 1] == '*' {\n168\t                    // ** matches any characters including slashes.\n169\t                    result.push_str(\".*\");\n170\t                    i += 2;\n171\t                } else {\n172\t                    // * matches any non-slash characters.\n173\t                    result.push_str(\"[^/]+\");\n174\t                    i += 1;\n175\t                }\n176\t            }\n177\t            c => {\n178\t                // Pass through regex metacharacters literally - regex::Regex::new\n179\t                // will handle escaping. We only need to escape backslashes for\n180\t                // the glob conversion.\n181\t                result.push(c);\n182\t                i += 1;\n183\t            }\n184\t        }\n185\t    }\n186\t\n187\t    // Only add end anchor, not start anchor (glob patterns match substrings).\n188\t    format!(\"{}$\", result)\n189\t}\n190\t\n191\t/// Match a model name against routing rules, returning the adapter to use.\n192\t///\n193\t/// Evaluates rules in order; the first matching rule determines the adapter.\n194\t/// If no rule matches, returns the default adapter.\n195\t///\n196\t/// # Arguments\n197\t///\n198\t/// * `model` - The model name to match (e.g., \"claude-sonnet-4-6\").\n199\t/// * `rules` - Ordered list of routing rules (first match wins).\n200\t/// * `default` - Fallback adapter when no rules match.\n201\t///\n202\t/// # Returns\n203\t///\n204\t/// * `Some(adapter)` - The adapter name to use.\n205\t/// * `None` - No rule matched and default is empty/invalid (caller should handle).\n206\t///\n207\t/// # Examples\n208\t///\n209\t/// ```\n210\t/// use needle::routing::match_adapter;\n211\t/// use needle::config::RoutingRule;\n212\t///\n213\t/// let rules = vec![\n214\t///     RoutingRule {\n215\t///         match_model: \"sonnet.*\".to_string(),\n216\t///         adapter: \"claude-print\".to_string(),\n217\t///     },\n218\t///     RoutingRule {\n219\t///         match_model: \"*\".to_string(),\n220\t///         adapter: \"default-adapter\".to_string(),\n221\t///     },\n222\t/// ];\n223\t///\n224\t/// // First rule matches.\n225\t/// assert_eq!(\n226\t///     match_adapter(\"sonnet-4-6\", &rules, \"fallback\"),\n227\t///     Some(\"claude-print\".to_string())\n228\t/// );\n229\t///\n230\t/// // Second rule (catch-all) matches.\n231\t/// assert_eq!(\n232\t///     match_adapter(\"other-model\", &rules, \"fallback\"),\n233\t///     Some(\"default-adapter\".to_string())\n234\t/// );\n235\t/// ```\n236\tpub fn match_adapter(model: &str, rules: &[RoutingRule], default: &str) -> Option<String> {\n237\t    // Compile rules and test in order (first match wins).\n238\t    for rule in rules {\n239\t        match CompiledRule::from_rule(rule) {\n240\t            Ok(compiled) => {\n241\t                if compiled.matches(model) {\n242\t                    return Some(compiled.adapter.clone());\n243\t                }\n244\t            }\n245\t            Err(e) => {\n246\t                // Log the error but continue with other rules.\n247\t                // Invalid patterns are skipped rather than failing the entire dispatch.\n248\t                tracing::warn!(\n249\t                    pattern = %rule.match_model,\n250\t                    error = %e,\n251\t                    \"invalid routing pattern — skipping rule\"\n252\t                );\n253\t            }\n254\t        }\n255\t    }\n256\t\n257\t    // No rule matched — use default if provided.\n258\t    if default.is_empty() {\n259\t        None\n260\t    } else {\n261\t        Some(default.to_string())\n262\t    }\n263\t}\n264\t\n265\t/// Match a model name against a single glob pattern using the glob crate.\n266\t///\n267\t/// This is a lower-level function that tests if a glob pattern matches a model name.\n268\t/// It uses the `glob` crate's Pattern type directly for glob-style pattern matching.\n269\t///\n270\t/// # Arguments\n271\t///\n272\t/// * `pattern` - Glob pattern to match (e.g., \"claude-*\", \"gpt-*\", \"*\").\n273\t/// * `model_name` - The model name to test against the pattern.\n274\t///\n275\t/// # Returns\n276\t///\n277\t/// * `Some(())` - The pattern matches the model name.\n278\t/// * `None` - The pattern does not match or is invalid.\n279\t///\n280\t/// # Edge Cases\n281\t///\n282\t/// * Empty pattern: Returns `None` (no match).\n283\t/// * Empty model name: Returns `None` (no match).\n284\t/// * Invalid glob pattern: Returns `None` (no match).\n285\t///\n286\t/// # Glob Pattern Syntax\n287\t///\n288\t/// * `*` - Matches any sequence of non-separator characters.\n289\t/// * `**` - Matches any sequence of characters, including path separators.\n290\t/// * `?` - Matches any single non-separator character.\n291\t/// * `[a-z]` - Matches any character in the bracket.\n292\t/// * `[!a-z]` - Matches any character not in the bracket.\n293\t///\n294\t/// # Examples\n295\t///\n296\t/// ```\n297\t/// use needle::routing::match_adapter_with_glob;\n298\t///\n299\t/// // Match with wildcard\n300\t/// assert!(match_adapter_with_glob(\"claude-*\", \"claude-sonnet-4-6\").is_some());\n301\t/// assert!(match_adapter_with_glob(\"claude-*\", \"claude-opus-4-6\").is_some());\n302\t/// assert!(match_adapter_with_glob(\"claude-*\", \"gpt-4\").is_none());\n303\t///\n304\t/// // Match with double wildcard\n305\t/// assert!(match_adapter_with_glob(\"**\", \"any-model\").is_some());\n306\t///\n307\t/// // Edge cases\n308\t/// assert!(match_adapter_with_glob(\"\", \"model\").is_none());\n309\t/// assert!(match_adapter_with_glob(\"pattern\", \"\").is_none());\n310\t/// ```\n311\tpub fn match_adapter_with_glob(pattern: &str, model_name: &str) -> Option<()> {\n312\t    // Handle edge cases\n313\t    if pattern.is_empty() || model_name.is_empty() {\n314\t        return None;\n315\t    }\n316\t\n317\t    // Use the glob crate to compile and match the pattern\n318\t    match glob::Pattern::new(pattern) {\n319\t        Ok(glob_pattern) => {\n320\t            // The glob crate's Pattern::matches takes a &str directly\n321\t            if glob_pattern.matches(model_name) {\n322\t                Some(())\n323\t            } else {\n324\t                None\n325\t            }\n326\t        }\n327\t        Err(_) => {\n328\t            // Invalid glob pattern\n329\t            None\n330\t        }\n331\t    }\n332\t}\n333\t\n334\t/// Match a model name against a glob pattern.\n335\t///\n336\t/// This function uses the `glob` crate's Pattern functionality to perform\n337\t/// glob-style pattern matching against model names.\n338\t///\n339\t/// # Arguments\n340\t///\n341\t/// * `pattern` - Glob pattern to match (e.g., \"claude-*\", \"gpt-*\", \"*\").\n342\t/// * `model_name` - The model name to test against the pattern.\n343\t///\n344\t/// # Returns\n345\t///\n346\t/// * `true` - The pattern matches the model name.\n347\t/// * `false` - The pattern does not match, pattern is invalid, or either argument is empty.\n348\t///\n349\t/// # Glob Pattern Syntax\n350\t///\n351\t/// * `*` - Matches any sequence of non-separator characters.\n352\t/// * `**` - Matches any sequence of characters, including path separators.\n353\t/// * `?` - Matches any single non-separator character.\n354\t/// * `[a-z]` - Matches any character in the bracket.\n355\t/// * `[!a-z]` - Matches any character not in the bracket.\n356\t///\n357\t/// # Examples\n358\t///\n359\t/// ```\n360\t/// use needle::routing::match_glob;\n361\t///\n362\t/// // Match with wildcard\n363\t/// assert!(match_glob(\"claude-*\", \"claude-sonnet-4-6\"));\n364\t/// assert!(match_glob(\"claude-*\", \"claude-opus-4-6\"));\n365\t/// assert!(!match_glob(\"claude-*\", \"gpt-4\"));\n366\t///\n367\t/// // Match with double wildcard\n368\t/// assert!(match_glob(\"**\", \"any-model\"));\n369\t///\n370\t/// // Edge cases\n371\t/// assert!(!match_glob(\"\", \"model\"));  // Empty pattern\n372\t/// assert!(!match_glob(\"pattern\", \"\"));  // Empty model name\n373\t/// ```\n374\tpub fn match_glob(pattern: &str, model_name: &str) -> bool {\n375\t    // Handle edge cases\n376\t    if pattern.is_empty() || model_name.is_empty() {\n377\t        return false;\n378\t    }\n379\t\n380\t    // Use the glob crate to compile and match the pattern\n381\t    match glob::Pattern::new(pattern) {\n382\t        Ok(glob_pattern) => glob_pattern.matches(model_name),\n383\t        Err(_) => false, // Invalid glob pattern\n384\t    }\n385\t}\n386\t\n387\t// Routing rule matcher for model-to-adapter dispatch.\n//!\n//! Provides pattern matching logic for routing rules: regex/glob patterns\n//! against model names, first-match-wins semantics, and default fallback.\n\nuse crate::config::RoutingRule;\nuse std::sync::Arc;\n\n/// Compiled routing rule with cached regex for efficient matching.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\nstruct CompiledRule {\n    /// Compiled regex matcher.\n    matcher: Arc<regex::Regex>,\n    /// Adapter to use on match.\n    adapter: String,\n}\n\nimpl CompiledRule {\n    /// Compile a routing rule into an efficient matcher.\n    ///\n    /// Supports both regex patterns (any valid regex) and glob-style patterns:\n    /// - `*` matches any single path segment (non-greedy `[^/]+`)\n    /// - `**` matches zero or more path segments (`.+?` with greedy quantifier)\n    /// - Literal `*` or `**` must be escaped as `\\*` or `\\*\\*`\n    fn from_rule(rule: &RoutingRule) -> Result<Self, regex::Error> {\n        let pattern = &rule.match_model;\n        let adapter = rule.adapter.clone();\n\n        // Convert glob patterns to regex if needed.\n        // If the pattern contains * or ** without proper regex escaping,\n        // treat it as a glob pattern and convert.\n        let regex_pattern = if needs_glob_conversion(pattern) {\n            convert_glob_to_regex(pattern)\n        } else {\n            pattern.clone()\n        };\n\n        let matcher = regex::Regex::new(&regex_pattern)?;\n\n        Ok(CompiledRule {\n            matcher: Arc::new(matcher),\n            adapter,\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Test if a model name matches this rule.\n    fn matches(&self, model: &str) -> bool {\n        self.matcher.is_match(model)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Check if a pattern is a glob pattern.\n///\n/// A simple heuristic that returns true if the pattern contains glob-style\n/// wildcards (`*` or `**`). This is a basic check that doesn't attempt to\n/// distinguish between glob and regex patterns - it just reports whether\n/// the pattern contains wildcard characters.\n///\n/// # Arguments\n///\n/// * `pattern` - The pattern string to check.\n///\n/// # Returns\n///\n/// * `true` if the pattern contains `*` or `**`.\n/// * `false` otherwise.\n///\n/// # Examples\n///\n/// ```\n/// use needle::routing::is_glob_pattern;\n///\n/// // Glob patterns with wildcards\n/// assert!(is_glob_pattern(\"*\"));\n/// assert!(is_glob_pattern(\"**\"));\n/// assert!(is_glob_pattern(\"gpt-*\"));\n/// assert!(is_glob_pattern(\"test/**\"));\n///\n/// // Non-glob patterns (no wildcards)\n/// assert!(!is_glob_pattern(\"exact-match\"));\n/// assert!(!is_glob_pattern(\"gpt-4\"));\n/// assert!(!is_glob_pattern(\"claude-sonnet\"));\n/// ```\npub fn is_glob_pattern(pattern: &str) -> bool {\n    pattern.contains('*')\n}\n\n/// Check if a pattern contains glob-style wildcards that need conversion.\n///\n/// Returns true if the pattern appears to be a glob pattern rather than\n/// a well-formed regex. The heuristic checks for:\n/// 1. Regex features: anchors (^$), character classes [], parentheses (),\n///    quantifiers +?{}, alternation |, or the regex wildcard sequence .*\n/// 2. If present, it's a regex pattern - no conversion needed\n/// 3. If absent, but * is present, it's a glob pattern - convert it\nfn needs_glob_conversion(pattern: &str) -> bool {\n    // First, check if it looks like a regex by looking for regex metacharacters.\n    // The key indicator is .* which is \"any character\" in regex but not in glob.\n    let has_regex_features = pattern.contains(|c| {\n        matches!(\n            c,\n            '^' | '$' | '(' | ')' | '[' | ']' | '{' | '}' | '+' | '?' | '|' | '\\\\'\n        )\n    }) || pattern.contains(\".*\");\n\n    if has_regex_features {\n        // Has clear regex features - treat as regex\n        return false;\n    }\n\n    // At this point, we have a simple pattern that might be glob or regex.\n    // If it contains unescaped * (and we already ruled out other regex chars),\n    // treat it as a glob pattern.\n    let chars: Vec<char> = pattern.chars().collect();\n    let mut i = 0;\n\n    while i < chars.len() {\n        if chars[i] == '\\\\' && i + 1 < chars.len() {\n            // Skip escaped character.\n            i += 2;\n            continue;\n        }\n        if chars[i] == '*' {\n            return true;\n        }\n        i += 1;\n    }\n\n    false\n}\n\n/// Convert glob-style pattern to regex.\n///\n/// Rules:\n/// - `*` alone → `.*` (match anything, catch-all)\n/// - `*` in other contexts → `[^/]+` (match any single segment, no slashes)\n/// - `**` → `.*` (match any characters including slashes, greedy)\n/// - Escaped `\\*` and `\\*\\*` treated literally\n/// - No implicit start anchor for glob patterns (unlike regex patterns)\nfn convert_glob_to_regex(glob: &str) -> String {\n    // Special case: * and ** should match anything (including empty).\n    if glob == \"*\" || glob == \"**\" {\n        return \"^.*$\".to_string();\n    }\n\n    let mut result = String::new();\n    let chars: Vec<char> = glob.chars().collect();\n    let mut i = 0;\n\n    while i < chars.len() {\n        match chars[i] {\n            '\\\\' => {\n                // Escaped character - pass through the backslash and the character.\n                // This ensures that \\* in the glob becomes \\* in the regex (literal asterisk).\n                if i + 1 < chars.len() {\n                    result.push('\\\\');\n                    result.push(chars[i + 1]);\n                    i += 2;\n                } else {\n                    // Trailing backslash - treat literally.\n                    result.push('\\\\');\n                    i += 1;\n                }\n            }\n            '*' => {\n                // Check for **.\n                if i + 1 < chars.len() && chars[i + 1] == '*' {\n                    // ** matches any characters including slashes.\n                    result.push_str(\".*\");\n                    i += 2;\n                } else {\n                    // * matches any non-slash characters.\n                    result.push_str(\"[^/]+\");\n                    i += 1;\n                }\n            }\n            c => {\n                // Pass through regex metacharacters literally - regex::Regex::new\n                // will handle escaping. We only need to escape backslashes for\n                // the glob conversion.\n                result.push(c);\n                i += 1;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Only add end anchor, not start anchor (glob patterns match substrings).\n    format!(\"{}$\", result)\n}\n\n/// Match a model name against routing rules, returning the adapter to use.\n///\n/// Evaluates rules in order; the first matching rule determines the adapter.\n/// If no rule matches, returns the default adapter.\n///\n/// # Arguments\n///\n/// * `model` - The model name to match (e.g., \"claude-sonnet-4-6\").\n/// * `rules` - Ordered list of routing rules (first match wins).\n/// * `default` - Fallback adapter when no rules match.\n///\n/// # Returns\n///\n/// * `Some(adapter)` - The adapter name to use.\n/// * `None` - No rule matched and default is empty/invalid (caller should handle).\n///\n/// # Examples\n///\n/// ```\n/// use needle::routing::match_adapter;\n/// use needle::config::RoutingRule;\n///\n/// let rules = vec![\n///     RoutingRule {\n///         match_model: \"sonnet.*\".to_string(),\n///         adapter: \"claude-print\".to_string(),\n///     },\n///     RoutingRule {\n///         match_model: \"*\".to_string(),\n///         adapter: \"default-adapter\".to_string(),\n///     },\n/// ];\n///\n/// // First rule matches.\n/// assert_eq!(\n///     match_adapter(\"sonnet-4-6\", &rules, \"fallback\"),\n///     Some(\"claude-print\".to_string())\n/// );\n///\n/// // Second rule (catch-all) matches.\n/// assert_eq!(\n///     match_adapter(\"other-model\", &rules, \"fallback\"),\n///     Some(\"default-adapter\".to_string())\n/// );\n/// ```\npub fn match_adapter(model: &str, rules: &[RoutingRule], default: &str) -> Option<String> {\n    // Compile rules and test in order (first match wins).\n    for rule in rules {\n        match CompiledRule::from_rule(rule) {\n            Ok(compiled) => {\n                if compiled.matches(model) {\n                    return Some(compiled.adapter.clone());\n                }\n            }\n            Err(e) => {\n                // Log the error but continue with other rules.\n                // Invalid patterns are skipped rather than failing the entire dispatch.\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    pattern = %rule.match_model,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"invalid routing pattern — skipping rule\"\n                );\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // No rule matched — use default if provided.\n    if default.is_empty() {\n        None\n    } else {\n        Some(default.to_string())\n    }\n}\n\n/// Match a model name against a single glob pattern using the glob crate.\n///\n/// This is a lower-level function that tests if a glob pattern matches a model name.\n/// It uses the `glob` crate's Pattern type directly for glob-style pattern matching.\n///\n/// # Arguments\n///\n/// * `pattern` - Glob pattern to match (e.g., \"claude-*\", \"gpt-*\", \"*\").\n/// * `model_name` - The model name to test against the pattern.\n///\n/// # Returns\n///\n/// * `Some(())` - The pattern matches the model name.\n/// * `None` - The pattern does not match or is invalid.\n///\n/// # Edge Cases\n///\n/// * Empty pattern: Returns `None` (no match).\n/// * Empty model name: Returns `None` (no match).\n/// * Invalid glob pattern: Returns `None` (no match).\n///\n/// # Glob Pattern Syntax\n///\n/// * `*` - Matches any sequence of non-separator characters.\n/// * `**` - Matches any sequence of characters, including path separators.\n/// * `?` - Matches any single non-separator character.\n/// * `[a-z]` - Matches any character in the bracket.\n/// * `[!a-z]` - Matches any character not in the bracket.\n///\n/// # Examples\n///\n/// ```\n/// use needle::routing::match_adapter_with_glob;\n///\n/// // Match with wildcard\n/// assert!(match_adapter_with_glob(\"claude-*\", \"claude-sonnet-4-6\").is_some());\n/// assert!(match_adapter_with_glob(\"claude-*\", \"claude-opus-4-6\").is_some());\n/// assert!(match_adapter_with_glob(\"claude-*\", \"gpt-4\").is_none());\n///\n/// // Match with double wildcard\n/// assert!(match_adapter_with_glob(\"**\", \"any-model\").is_some());\n///\n/// // Edge cases\n/// assert!(match_adapter_with_glob(\"\", \"model\").is_none());\n/// assert!(match_adapter_with_glob(\"pattern\", \"\").is_none());\n/// ```\npub fn match_adapter_with_glob(pattern: &str, model_name: &str) -> Option<()> {\n    // Handle edge cases\n    if pattern.is_empty() || model_name.is_empty() {\n        return None;\n    }\n\n    // Use the glob crate to compile and match the pattern\n    match glob::Pattern::new(pattern) {\n        Ok(glob_pattern) => {\n            // The glob crate's Pattern::matches takes a &str directly\n            if glob_pattern.matches(model_name) {\n                Some(())\n            } else {\n                None\n            }\n        }\n        Err(_) => {\n            // Invalid glob pattern\n            None\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Match a model name against a glob pattern.\n///\n/// This function uses the `glob` crate's Pattern functionality to perform\n/// glob-style pattern matching against model names.\n///\n/// # Arguments\n///\n/// * `pattern` - Glob pattern to match (e.g., \"claude-*\", \"gpt-*\", \"*\").\n/// * `model_name` - The model name to test against the pattern.\n///\n/// # Returns\n///\n/// * `true` - The pattern matches the model name.\n/// * `false` - The pattern does not match, pattern is invalid, or either argument is empty.\n///\n/// # Glob Pattern Syntax\n///\n/// * `*` - Matches any sequence of non-separator characters.\n/// * `**` - Matches any sequence of characters, including path separators.\n/// * `?` - Matches any single non-separator character.\n/// * `[a-z]` - Matches any character in the bracket.\n/// * `[!a-z]` - Matches any character not in the bracket.\n///\n/// # Examples\n///\n/// ```\n/// use needle::routing::match_glob;\n///\n/// // Match with wildcard\n/// assert!(match_glob(\"claude-*\", \"claude-sonnet-4-6\"));\n/// assert!(match_glob(\"claude-*\", \"claude-opus-4-6\"));\n/// assert!(!match_glob(\"claude-*\", \"gpt-4\"));\n///\n/// // Match with double wildcard\n/// assert!(match_glob(\"**\", \"any-model\"));\n///\n/// // Edge cases\n/// assert!(!match_glob(\"\", \"model\"));  // Empty pattern\n/// assert!(!match_glob(\"pattern\", \"\"));  // Empty model name\n/// ```\npub fn match_glob(pattern: &str, model_name: &str) -> bool {\n    // Handle edge cases\n    if pattern.is_empty() || model_name.is_empty() {\n        return false;\n    }\n\n    // Use the glob crate to compile and match the pattern\n    match glob::Pattern::new(pattern) {\n        Ok(glob_pattern) => glob_pattern.matches(model_name),\n        Err(_) => false, // Invalid glob pattern\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Tests\n//
